label: Core Concepts
desc: 15 interview questions covering Fundamentals, FlowFiles, Processors, Monitoring and more.

subs.label: FlowFiles
subs.desc: You can certainly add attributes to your FlowFiles at any time — that's the whole point of separating metadata from the actual data.

subs.label: Processors
subs.desc: The Processor is the main component in NiFi that actually works on the FlowFile content, helping create, send, receive, transform, route, split, merge, and otherwise process FlowFiles.

subs.label: Monitoring
subs.desc: What is a Reporting Task? What is bulleting and how does it help in NiFi?

subs.label: Extensibility
subs.desc: NiFi is implemented in the Java programming language and allows extensions (processors, controller services, and reporting tasks) to be implemented in Java.

subs.label: Architecture
subs.desc: Huge volumes of data can transit through a DataFlow because, as data moves through NiFi, only a pointer to the data is passed around (referred to as a FlowFile).

subs.label: Flow Control
subs.desc: Sometimes a producer system is faster than the consumer system, so messages are consumed more slowly than they're produced.

subs.label: Templates
subs.desc: A template is a re-usable workflow that you can import and export within the same or different NiFi instances.

subs.label: Security
subs.desc: What happens if you have stored a password in a dataflow and create a template out of it?

subs.label: Configuration
subs.desc: What is a NiFi custom properties registry?

subs.label: Clustering
subs.desc: Does NiFi work as a Master-Slave architecture?
